_meta.conventions: Every figure carries its source URL, publisher, publication date (null when the page shows none), sourceType ('primary' = the retailer, government body or study author itself; 'secondary' = a guide, aggregator or press report), and 'confirmed'. confirmed=true means the figure was read directly from the page or document on 2026-09-30. confirmed=false means it came from a search-engine extract of that page because the page itself refused automated access (HTTP 403 or timeout); treat those as likely-but-unverified. Null means no published figure was found, and the note says so. Retail prices are shelf prices on the retrieval date and move with sales.
_meta.spelling: American spelling in our own words; product and publication names are quoted as published.

irsPub527PartOfHome.rule: If you rent part of your home, you divide shared expenses (mortgage interest, taxes, heat, electricity) between rental and personal use as though they were two separate properties. Any reasonable method is allowed, and the two most common are the number of rooms and square footage; the IRS adds that some items, such as water, can reasonably be split by the number of people using them. Expenses that belong only to the rented part, such as painting the rented room or liability insurance for renting it, are fully rental expenses. The rented part may be depreciated. No part of the first phone line is deductible.
irsPub527PartOfHome.example: A 12 x 15 ft (180 sq ft) room in an 1,800 sq ft house gives 10% of shared expenses as rental: a $600 heating bill yields $60 rental and $540 nondeductible personal.

source.date: 2025 tax year (for use in preparing 2025 returns)

irsPub527PartOfHome.note: Chapter 4, Special Situations, 'Renting Part of Property'. Rent below fair rental falls under the not-for-profit rules, where income is still reported but rental expenses cannot be deducted.

ofgemTDCV.note: The decision sets bands by consumption, not by household size. The common labels (low = flat or 1 bed with 1-2 people, medium = 2-3 bed with 2-3 people, high = 4+ bed with 4-5 people) come from suppliers' and comparison sites' guides and are not in this decision.

source.publisher: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero (NEED consumption data tables 2026, Tables 13c and 14c)

medianConsumptionByNumberOfAdults2024.note: Read directly from the spreadsheet. We derived the increments by subtracting adjacent medians. They are cross-sectional (bigger households also live in bigger homes), so they overstate what one lodger adds to a fixed home, especially for gas, which follows floor area. A lodger joining a 1-adult home is closest to the 1-to-2 step on electricity.

energySavingTrustExtraPersonFigure.note: No Energy Saving Trust figure for what one extra occupant adds was found. A secondary guide claims each extra adult adds about £190-£390 a year, but that is a derived figure and is not recorded as published.

spareRoomTimeToFill.note: SpareRoom publishes no average time to fill or let a room. Its only related statistic is marketing ('someone finds a flatmate every 3 minutes'), plus user testimonials (rooms let in 3 to 10 days) that are anecdotes. Its statistics page (https://www.spareroom.co.uk/statistics/) covers rents and supply, not void length.

englandRightToRent.scope: England only. No check is required in Wales, Scotland or Northern Ireland. The duty covers a resident landlord who takes in a lodger.
englandRightToRent.lodgerDefinition: Someone who takes a room within accommodation they share with their landlord (the owner or an occupier).

onlineCheck.how: For tenants who are not British or Irish citizens: the tenant generates a 9-character share code, and the landlord enters it with the tenant's date of birth at gov.uk/view-right-to-rent. The code is valid for 90 days. British and Irish citizens cannot get a share code; their original documents are checked instead, or a Digital Verification Service is used.
onlineCheck.feeNote: The GOV.UK service page and the Home Office landlord's guide ask for no payment and state no fee, but neither says in so many words that the check is free. Secondary guides (e.g. Selectra, Landlord Studio) state it is free. Commercial Digital Verification Services, which are optional for British and Irish passport holders, charge their own fees.

fastPaymentOptionGBP.condition: First breach only, paid within 21 calendar days of the notice (a 30% discount).

civilPenalties.note: A new code of practice takes effect 2026-10-01, the day after retrieval. It keeps the same penalty amounts and mainly adds digital documents and Digital Verification Service rules. The pre-2024 amounts come from secondary law-firm summaries (e.g. Shoosmiths), not a primary page. Criminal prosecution, with possible imprisonment, remains available for knowing breaches.

uncertain: Most retail prices (Argos, Currys UK and IE, Best Buy Canada, Home Depot Canada, Coppel, Liverpool, Walmart MX) come from search-engine extracts because those sites blocked automated fetches; they are marked confirmed=false. Prices confirmed directly: MicksGarage twin tub (EUR 149.99), BuyItDirect.ie table-top dishwashers, and Danby list prices.
Harvey Norman Ireland and DID Electrical do not appear to sell twin tubs, portable washers, 3 kg dryers or table-top dishwashers (DID verified from its full catalog; Harvey Norman not verifiable).

Mexican 'secadora compacta' at mass retail is usually a heatless centrifugal spin extractor (Koblenz SCK-60), not a heated tumble dryer. Search extracts also showed some 'Genérica' units near MXN 1,000 on Liverpool that may be garment-bag dryers.
NAR has not published an HVAC cost-recovered figure since 2019 (85%). The current figure is from Cost vs. Value 2025 (72%), a different publisher and methodology (heat-pump conversion).
The Zillow central-air premium (2.5%, $5,486) dates from 2018. No dishwasher sale-premium study exists in a primary source.
Mover figures are estimate ranges from comparison sites and movers, not quotes. MoveHub prices every route in GBP. The Three Movers Canada-Mexico range does not state its currency.
The NEED per-adult increments are cross-sectional medians and not a controlled 'one lodger added' measurement.
No official source states outright that the Home Office online right-to-rent check is free; it asks for no payment, and secondary sources say it is free.
No published average void or time-to-fill for a lodger room exists from SpareRoom.
